attributes.output.value: {"summary": "This is a short-form sample Software Services Agreement between a Customer and a Provider covering a 12-month term with a single attached Statement of Work. It addresses fees, IP, confidentiality, mutual indemnification, data protection, Delaware governing law, and mandatory binding arbitration. The contract is skeletal and resembles a low-friction template: many critical commercial and operational protections (SLAs, acceptance, data security specifics, insurance, transition assistance, survival, notice mechanics) are absent, and several key clauses contain ambiguous or one-sided language that materially favors the Provider.", "risks": ["Asymmetric termination rights: Clause 3 lets the Provider terminate immediately for a Customer payment breach, while the Customer must give 90 days' written notice to terminate for convenience ('Provider may terminate immediately if Customer breaches payment obligations'), creating an imbalance.", "Customer has no post-term right to use deliverables: Clause 4 grants only 'a limited license to use the deliverables during the term,' so all Customer access to deliverables ends at termination, with no perpetual license, transition period, or work-product ownership carve-out.", "High default interest and no invoice dispute mechanism: Clause 2 imposes '1.5 percent per month' (~18% APR) on late pay with no process to dispute amounts in good faith, exposing the Customer to penalty interest even on contested invoices.", "Liability cap lacks standard carve-outs: Clause 8 caps each party's total liability at 'fees paid in the prior 12 months' with no exclusions for breach of confidentiality, IP indemnification, data breach, gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud, which may be unenforceable in many jurisdictions and leaves the Customer under-protected for the most harmful breaches.", "'Reasonable care' confidentiality standard is vague and indefinite: Clause 5 ('protect the other's confidential information using reasonable care') lacks a defined duration, mandatory return/destruction, permitted disclosures (legal/regulatory), and standard exceptions (publicly available, independently developed, lawfully obtained), creating ambiguity for both sides.", "Broad and unbalanced indemnification: Clause 9 requires Customer to indemnify for 'claims arising from Customer data' with no scope limits, IP exclusions, or control-of-defense rights, while the Provider's IP indemnity lacks exclusions (e.g., combinations, modifications, use beyond specifications) and does not expressly require defense or settlement consent.", "Vague data protection obligations: Clause 10 commits the parties only to 'reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards' and compliance with 'applicable law,' with no reference to GDPR/CCPA/HIPAA, no breach notification timeline, no data return/deletion obligations, no subprocessor controls, and no audit rights—well below market expectations for 2026.", "Mandatory binding arbitration without injunctive carve-out: Clause 12 forces 'binding arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware' for 'unresolved disputes,' with no exception for emergency/injunctive relief, no specified arbitral forum or rules (e.g., AAA/JAMS), no class-action waiver, and no fee-shifting, which can disadvantage the smaller party.", "Forced venue and governing law may increase Customer's litigation cost: Clause 11 (Delaware law) and Clause 12 (Wilmington arbitration) together impose a single, Provider-favorable forum that may be inconvenient and costly for an out-of-state Customer.", "Force majeure is undefined and has no mitigation or notice duty: Clause 14 ('delays caused by events beyond its reasonable control') does not enumerate events, require prompt notice, or obligate the non-performing party to mitigate or terminate after extended suspension, leaving the Customer without a clear exit during prolonged Provider outages.", "No acceptance criteria, SLAs, or credits: There are no service levels, uptime guarantees, response/resolution times, or acceptance testing procedures, so the Customer has no measurable remedy for deficient performance beyond the weak warranty in Clause 6.", "No survival, notices, anti-corruption, insurance, transition assistance, or change-order mechanics: These standard protections are entirely missing, creating risk for both parties and especially the Customer at termination.", "Entire Agreement clause may inadvertently swallow missing protections: Clause 15 ('supersedes all prior agreements') means that nothing in the SOW, exhibits, or pre-contract discussions can fill these gaps if there is no order-of-precedence provision."], "key_clauses": ["Services (Clause 1): 'Provider will deliver the software services described in the attached Statement of Work. Customer will provide reasonable access to its systems and data needed for delivery.' Obligations are delegable to the SOW and the Customer's cooperation duty is subjective.", "Fees and Payment (Clause 2): 'pay the fees listed in the Statement of Work within 30 days after invoice. Late payments accrue interest at 1.5 percent per month.' Net-30 with punitive default interest and no dispute mechanism.", "Term and Termination (Clause 3): '12 months' initial term, '90 days written notice' termination for convenience, and asymmetric immediate termination right for payment default by the Provider.", "Intellectual Property (Clause 4): 'Provider retains all rights in its software, tools, and preexisting materials. Customer receives a limited license to use the deliverables during the term.' No perpetual license, no ownership of work product, no license back to Provider of Customer data.", "Confidentiality (Clause 5): 'protect the other's confidential information using reasonable care and will not disclose it without prior written consent.' Vague standard, no duration, no exceptions, no return/destruction.", "Warranties and Disclaimer (Clauses 6–7): A narrow professional-services warranty paired with a broad 'as is' disclaimer for everything else; no fitness-for-purpose, results, or non-infringement warranties beyond the limited indemnity.", "Limitation of Liability (Clause 8): 'Neither party will be liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages. Each party's total liability is limited to fees paid in the prior 12 months.' Mutual cap with no carve-outs.", "Indemnification (Clause 9): IP infringement indemnity by Provider with no carve-outs, and a broad Customer indemnity for 'claims arising from Customer data.'", "Data Protection (Clause 10): Generic obligation to comply with 'applicable law' and maintain 'reasonable' safeguards; no specific regimes, breach notice, or audit rights.", "Dispute Resolution (Clause 12): 'first attempt to resolve disputes through good faith negotiation. Unresolved disputes will be submitted to binding arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware.' No injunctive carve-out, no specified rules."], "recommendations": ["Add a Survival clause and a perpetual, royalty-free license (or ownership transfer) of Customer-specific work product and configurations so the Customer can continue using deliverables after termination; otherwise the 'during the term' license in Clause 4 creates a lockout risk.", "Make termination symmetric: permit the Customer to terminate immediately for material breach (including Provider security or SLA failures) and require mutual notice/cure periods; alternatively, limit the Provider's immediate termination right in Clause 3 to material, uncured payment defaults and align notice/cure mechanics for both sides.", "Add invoice dispute mechanics to Clause 2: permit the Customer to withhold disputed amounts in good faith while timely paying undisputed amounts, and suspend interest accrual on amounts under dispute until resolved.", "Negotiate specific carve-outs to the liability cap in Clause 8 for (i) breach of confidentiality, (ii) IP indemnity obligations, (iii) data security/privacy breaches, (iv) gross negligence, willful misconduct, and fraud; consider a higher super-cap (e.g., 2–3x fees) for these categories, and ensure the cap does not limit injunctive or equitable remedies.", "Strengthen Clause 5: define Confidential Information, require return or certified destruction within 30 days of termination, include standard exceptions (publicly known, independently developed, lawfully known, required by law), impose specific confidentiality obligations on personnel and subcontractors, and set a minimum 3–5 year confidentiality survival period.", "Tighten Clause 9: limit the Customer's data indemnity to third-party claims arising from Customer-provided data used as directed by the Customer, exclude claims caused by Provider's modification or combination, and give the indemnified party control of defense with the indemnifying party's obligation to defend and obtain consent for settlements; add standard Provider IP indemnity exclusions (e.g., use beyond specifications, modifications, combinations) and require replacement/licensing/remedy obligations.", "Replace the generic Clause 10 with a Data Protection Schedule that specifies applicable regimes (GDPR/CCPA/HIPAA as relevant), breach notification within 24–72 hours, subprocessor approval/flow-down obligations, data return/deletion on termination, security audits/penetration tests, and insurance-backed coverage for privacy incidents.", "Add SLAs and acceptance: include measurable service levels (uptime, response, resolution), service credits as liquidated remedies, and an acceptance testing procedure with deemed-acceptance criteria tied to the SOW.", "Add an Insurance clause requiring the Provider to maintain commercial general liability, cyber/tech E&O, and professional liability insurance at specified limits, with the Customer named as additional insured where appropriate and certificates provided on request.", "Add a Force Majeure framework in Clause 14: enumerate qualifying events, require prompt written notice, impose mitigation and information duties, and allow the Customer to terminate (without liability) after a defined suspension period (e.g., 30–60 days).", "Enhance Clause 12: specify the arbitral institution and rules (AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules or JAMS), arbitral seat/venue, language, confidentiality of proceedings, permit a carve-out for injunctive or equitable relief in court, add a class-action waiver, and provide for award of attorneys' fees to the prevailing party.", "Add a detailed Notices clause (addresses, deemed delivery methods), an Order of Precedence provision (Agreement > SOW > exhibits), a Change Management process for SOW modifications, Transition Assistance obligations, Anti-Corruption/Export Compliance, Non-Solicitation (limited duration), and Audit Rights for security and financial/compliance purposes.", "Narrow Clause 11 to a neutral jurisdiction tied to the Customer's principal place of business (or make it mutual/negotiable), and ensure consistency between governing law and dispute resolution venue."]}
